name: Myelocystocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Myelocystocele

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic mass over the spinal region at birth
MRI demonstrating a dilated central canal forming a cystic cavity continuous with the spinal cord
Neurological impairment consistent with spinal cord tethering or dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a cystic spinal mass at birth with confirmatory MRI findings of a dilated central canal cystic cavity continuous with the spinal cord
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cystic spinal mass at the lumbosacral region
pathognomonic.notes: Visible or palpable cystic swelling present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dilated central canal cyst continuous with spinal cord on imaging
searchTerms: fluid-filled cavity continuous with spinal cord

common.notes: Variable degree of paresis or paralysis

searchTerms: sensory loss in feet and legs

common.notes: Pain or neurological deterioration due to spinal cord tethering

occasional.notes: May occur with associated neural tube defects

occasional.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata overlying the lesion (e.g., skin dimpling, hairy patch)
occasional.notes: May be present but not always
searchTerms: skin dimpling or hairy patch on back

occasional.notes: Especially in older children or adults with tethered cord

searchTerms: bowel control problems from nerve damage
difficulty with bowel movements due to nerve issues

rare.notes: Increased muscle tone due to spinal cord involvement
searchTerms: increased muscle tone in lower limbs

imaging: MRI showing dilated central canal cyst continuous with spinal cord
Ultrasound may detect cystic spinal mass prenatally or postnatally
other: Physical examination revealing cystic mass over spinal region
Neurological examination showing lower limb deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Open spinal defect with exposed neural tissue
Absence of intact skin covering the lesion
More severe neurological deficits at birth
Cystic spinal mass containing meninges only without neural tissue
MRI shows absence of spinal cord involvement

redFlags: Signs of infection or rupture of cystic mass
references: Radiographics. Myelocystocele: MRI findings and clinical features. 2015.
